Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited about Redwood's throughput profile. We are evaluating a 3-year commitment (expected volume ~100M tokens/month) and our procurement team has two asks before we can move to legal: 

1) A fixed price preservation for the term — we need a formal guarantee that unit pricing will not increase by more than 3% total over the 3-year term (effectively a ceiling on annual increases).
2) A hard uplift cap on negotiated overage rates — Phoenix prefers a maximum annual uplift of 8% for baseline pricing adjustments.

Attached is a one-page summary of what we need (Phoenix_Term_Summary_v3.pdf). Can Redwood confirm whether these are within scope for a standard enterprise addendum, or whether this requires executive signoff / a special-rate exception?

Leonard

Subject: [Escalation] Exec signoff needed: Phoenix AI 3yr preserve + 8% uplift cap

Team —

Quick thread: Phoenix AI (DL-2028-4097) is asking for two commitment controls that are outside our default terms:
- A cumulative price preservation clause that limits total price increases across the 3-year term to a maximum of 3% (they framed it as "no more than 3% total over term").
- A hard uplift cap on negotiated annual overage adjustments at 8% per year.

Deal economics: ~100M tokens/month baseline; projected ARR if accepted ~ $5.4M (year one). They are willing to sign a 36-month commitment if we provide these protections and an express renewal protection clause preventing step-changes >4% at renewal without 60 days notice.

Options I see:
A) Approve as-is (offer the preservation + uplift cap) in exchange for a modestly higher minimum commitment and an up-front partial prepayment (2 months equivalent) to offset pricing risk.
B) Counter with a looser preservation (cap at 5% cumulative) and uplift cap at 12% with an earn-in (quarterly review).
C) Deny and route back to procurement — likely kills the deal.

Attachments: Phoenix_Term_Summary_v3.pdf, SOW-PhxAI-3yr.xlsx (summary economics included).

Request: Ben/Marissa/Kim — can you review and advise whether we have authority to accept A or if you prefer B? If A, I need Exec signoff to commit to the protective language in the commercial addendum. The customer timeline is tight: procurement wants a doc in their hands by end-of-week (Friday).

Olga

Subject: Re: [Escalation] Exec signoff needed: Phoenix AI 3yr preserve + 8% uplift cap

Olga / team —

I reviewed the SOW and sketched the P&L impact for a three-year lock. High-level: allowing a 3% cumulative cap with no additional protections materially increases our exposure to inflation and GPU cost drift, given their volume. I’m comfortable approving Option A only if these conditions are added:
- Two-month prepayment at contract execution (applied to year one).
- A contractual escape: automatic reprice trigger if model-inference hardware costs increase >15% sustained over two consecutive quarters.
- Annual usage reconciliation clause with a true-up capped at their uplift amount.

If the customer will accept those, approve Option A with Exec signoff. If Phoenix pushes back on the prepayment or escape clause, move to Option B and present a compromise.

Ben
SVP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
